text:
AHNS (AAAI 2024) supports adaptive hardness, but its evidence does not endorse a generic easy-to-hard curriculum. Experiments use matrix factorization with BPR, comparing uniform RNS, hardest-candidate DNS, fixed-hardness DNS(M,N), and curriculum CuCo. AHNS conditions hardness on the positive score; observed hardness decreases during training. False-negative mitigation is inferred from hardness/performance trajectories rather than measured false-negative labels. Per-epoch timing finds overhead comparable to DNS, while uniform sampling remains fastest. [AHNS paper](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.05191v1)

R2NS (WWW 2026) more directly separates controls: uniform sampling; DNS+ randomly selecting from top-5 among 100 candidates; and U-DNS+, adding 30 uniform warm-start epochs. Its No-CRR ablation removes progressive hardness while retaining other components: Beauty Recall@10 falls from 0.0983 to 0.0759, Toys 0.1081 to 0.0963, Sports 0.0492 to 0.0481. Separate No-WS, No-GR, and No-DI ablations address warm-start, global recall, and random-candidate diversity. Evidence therefore extends beyond general hard-negative motivation, although curriculum benefits vary substantially. Stochastic selection is motivated as false-negative mitigation; no direct false-negative-rate or duplicate-candidate ablation is reported. Mining efficiency receives complexity analysis, not wall-clock benchmarking. Tested backbones exclude BERT4Rec; BCE/BPR results do not establish transfer to masked-item training. [R2NS paper](https://renzhaochun.github.io/assets/pdf/WWW_2026_Camera_Ready.pdf)

Useful proposed controls: uniform, constant stochastic top-M, warm-start plus constant top-M, and warm-start plus progressive top-M, holding unique candidate count and updates fixed. Record candidate collisions, positive/history exclusions, hardness distributions, mining time, GPU-seconds, and validation HR@10. For BERT4Rec, mine from masked-position representations with targets hidden; distinguish sampled-loss changes from full-softmax training. These are experimental recommendations, not established findings from either paper.
